newsitem.title: USA: Abundant orange supplies seen squeezing FCOJ price.
newsitem.headline: Abundant orange supplies seen squeezing FCOJ price.

text.p: Thursday's limit-down move in FCOJ futures is only the beginning of a long0term downtrend that could pressure the market into the 50.00 cent per lb range, analysts said.

"The fact is, we've never had a situation where there are record ending stocks anticipated by a record crop when retail prices remain relatively high and Brazil is having record output," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said. "Plus, the specs are heavily long."

Thursday, FCOJ prices fell to a more than four-year low on a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida orange crop. The benchmark September contract fell to a new low of 69.50 cents, its weakest level since trading at a monthly average of 69.10 cents in February 1993, analysts said.
Florida-based Citrus Consulting International does not release its number to the public but industry sources said the forecast came in at a record 253.0 million 90-lb boxes.
USDA pegged the current crop at a record 225.7 million boxes.

"This crop report will put pressure on prices all year," a broker said, pegging technical support at 65.45 cents and longer term fundamental support between 60.00 and 50.00 cents for the nearby contract.
"Look to work into these numbers on technicals but fundamentally it could take more time," the broker said.
A heavy speculative long position will also keep prices under technical pressure. As of Aug 8, the speculators were 77.7 percent long the market.

"The speculative commitment in the market is in excess of 77 percent," Jimmy Quinn, a floor source with AG Edwards, said. "With the specs long before the report and the report coming out negative, there is quite a bit of liquidation that needs to be done before the market turns around."

But Florida Department of Citrus economist Philip Lesser said the market is not likely to sustain historically low prices hit on Thursday. "Now is the time to take your equity profits and go long orange juice," he said.
USDA said Brazil will produce a record 1.25 million tonnes of orange juice in 1997/98, up from 1.14 million tonnes produced this year.
